issue: Rule-recall items are labeled skill "analysis" and difficulty 3. Item 09 asks only for the testing order (lowest incremental EPS first, a fact the lesson and fc7 state outright). Items 06 and 26 ask only whether an out-of-the-money option or warrant (exercise price above average market price) is included. That is remembering/understanding, two levels below analysis.
evidence: 09: given X = 1.20 and Y = 3.40, the answer follows directly from the rule "most dilutive first"; nothing is computed. 06: exercise $50 > average $45 -> excluded. 26: exercise $30 > average $25 -> 0 shares; the stem does not even give the number of options. These three items, plus the over-labels in the companion S3 finding, push the practice pool to 13/28 = 46% "analysis". That overstates the module's contribution to the Blueprint analysis target (35-45%).
source: AICPA 2026 Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill definitions (Remembering & Understanding vs. Analysis); content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel far-eps-09 and far-eps-26 to skill "remembering" with difficulty 1, and far-eps-06 to "remembering" (or at most "application") with difficulty 1. Write genuine analysis items to replace them (see the coverage finding).

issue: Single-step computations are labeled skill "analysis" and/or difficulty 3, one level too high. As a result the practice set's labeled difficulty runs backwards: the easiest items (22-29) are tagged hardest, while richer items such as 01, 10 and 13 are tagged 2.
evidence: Each item is one formula application. 18: (500,000-50,000)/100,000. 22: (500,000-60,000)/100,000. 23: 100,000+15,000-2,500. 24: (100,000+6,000)x2. 25: 10,000-200,000/25. 27: 50,000x0.75. 29: 200,000x1.1. 20: 337,500/120,000. 16 has the same structure as 04, yet 04 is tagged difficulty 2 and 16 is tagged 3. Item 29 is the same computation as the lesson pre-question far-eps-pre1, but it is labeled analysis, difficulty 3.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions; content/sections/far.yaml skillAllocation
fix: Relabel to skill "application" for 18, 20, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27 and 29. Set difficulty to 1 for 25, 27 and 29, and to 2 for 16, 18, 20, 22, 23 and 24.

issue: Explanations are thin or circular. The distractor rationales are bare imperatives or "Not the computation." and never say what error produces the number. The item-level explanations restate the rule without the computation.
evidence: "Not the computation." appears on 22c, 22d, 23c, 24b, 25c and 29c. "That is not the rule." appears on 26d, and "That is not the test." on 28b and 28d. Other rationales are fragments: 17a "Weight by time.", 17d "Weight both changes." (101,000 actually comes from weighting the Oct 1 issue for 6/12), 21a "Weight from the issue date.", 24a "Restate for the split." (206,000 leaves the split off the July shares), 29a "Restate the full year." The item-level explanations of 18, 21, 22, 23, 25, 27, 28 and 29 show no numbers. Compare the house standard in 01, 08 and x1-07, which give the rule plus the full computation.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 4 (explanations teach)
fix: For each distractor, state the specific error and reproduce its number. Examples: 22c "$4.70 deducts only half the dividend (30,000)"; 22d "$5.60 adds the 60,000 instead of subtracting it"; 25c "2,500 divides the spread by the exercise price"; 24a "206,000 = 200,000 + 12,000x6/12, which fails to double the July shares". Add the full computation to each item-level explanation, e.g. 18: (500,000 - 50,000) / 100,000 = $4.50.

issue: Some distractor rationales misstate the arithmetic that produces the distractor, or describe an incoherent error.
evidence: 01(d) 64,000 is explained as weighting the issuance 4 months and the treasury purchase 8 months. That reversal gives 60,000 + 12,000x4/12 - 6,000x8/12 = 60,000, not 64,000. 64,000 = 60,000 + 8,000 - 6,000x8/12, i.e. the treasury shares weighted 8 months. 02(c) 50,833 = 50,000 + 5,000x2/12. Time-weighting a dividend distributed March 1 of the following year would add 0 shares to the current year, so no "time-weighting" misconception yields 50,833. 10(d) writes "90,000 x 6/12 + 270,000 x 6/12 = 180,000 + 7,500". The total of 187,500 is right, but the equation is garbled; it should read 45,000 + 135,000 + 7,500.
fix: 01(d): change the rationale to "This removes the treasury shares for 8 months (May-Dec) instead of 4: 60,000 + 8,000 - 4,000", or change the option to 60,000 to match the existing "reversed" rationale. 02(c): replace 50,833 with 54,167, explained as "Treats the dividend as if distributed March 1 of the current year: 50,000 + 5,000 x 10/12". 10(d): fix the parenthetical.

issue: The practice pool repeats the same fact the same way several times, while high-yield variants go untested (see the coverage finding).
evidence: Cumulative undeclared preferred deducted in basic EPS: 18 and 22 both use NI $500,000 and 100,000 shares (dividend $50,000 vs $60,000). The same structure appears again in exam items far-eps-03 and far-x1-22, in far-x1-07, in TBS far-tbs-x1-eps and in fc2. Treasury stock method incremental shares: 04, 16 and 25 (04 and 16 share the average-vs-year-end-price distractor), plus both TBSs. Out-of-the-money options: 06 and 26. After-tax interest add-back: 05, 20 and 27, plus far-x1-08 and both TBSs. Item 27 uses exactly the lesson faded example's numbers ($1,000,000, 5%, 25% -> 37,500). Convertible preferred antidilution: chk2, 19 and 28 (incremental EPS vs basic, all antidilutive). Full-year shares with a retroactive split or dividend: pre1, 02 and 29 (29 repeats pre1 with a dividend instead of a split). Weighted average with issue plus repurchase: 01, 17 and 23 (23 is the lesson worked example without the split). cues.md also flags 04~16 (Jaccard 0.67) and chk1~22.
source: Review brief section 2, per-MCQ check 7 (same fact tested >3 times)
fix: Replace 22, 25, 26, 27, 28 and 29 with the missing scenarios listed in the coverage finding. Keep one item per cluster in the practice pool.

issue: No MCQ or TBS tests several high-yield diluted-EPS scenarios that the exam commonly uses. The practice set has almost no genuine analysis-level items.
evidence: Not tested anywhere in the module: (1) a convertible bond or option issued mid-year, which needs partial-year weighting of the incremental shares and the interest add-back. The lesson states "or issuance date, if later", but no item practices it. (2) An actual conversion or exercise during the year, with potential shares before the conversion and actual shares after it. (3) An MCQ needing a final diluted EPS with two or more potential securities, ranked and sequentially tested; only the TBSs do this. (4) A net loss, where diluted EPS equals basic EPS; it is touched only indirectly by 14. (5) Convertible bonds issued at a discount, where the add-back is interest expense including amortization, net of tax. Skill mix: once the over-labels are corrected, analysis-level practice items fall to roughly 4/28 (chk2-style dilution tests, 08, 14 and x1-08). That is far below the Blueprint analysis share of 35-45%.
source: ASC 260-10-45 (treasury stock and if-converted methods: potential shares counted from the later of period start or issuance; conversions during the period); ASC 260-10-45-18 to 45-20 (control number/loss); AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint skill allocation
fix: Add 4-6 practice MCQs at application/analysis level covering items (1)-(5). Use them to replace the redundant items flagged in the redundancy finding (22, 25, 26, 27, 28, 29).

issue: The lesson never teaches the control-number rule (income from continuing operations), the treatment of a loss, or contingently issuable shares. Practice items far-eps-14 and far-eps-15 test these. The flowchart's "Start: basic EPS ... Does it lower EPS?" leaves open which EPS line governs.
evidence: Searching lesson.md for "control", "continuing operations" (it appears only in the presentation bullet), "loss" and "contingent" finds no teaching of these rules. Following the lesson in item 14's fact pattern (loss from continuing operations, net income from a gain on discontinued operations), a student would test dilution against net income and include the potential shares. That is wrong under ASC 260-10-45-18/-19.
source: ASC 260-10-45-18 to 45-20 (control number; loss from continuing operations); ASC 260-10-45-48 (contingently issuable shares in diluted EPS)
fix: Add two bullets to "Diluted EPS". First: "The dilution test uses income from continuing operations (the control number). If that is a loss, all potential shares are antidilutive and diluted EPS = basic EPS for every line." Second: "Contingently issuable shares: include in diluted EPS if the conditions would be met if period-end were the end of the contingency period; include in basic EPS only once all conditions are met." Add a key takeaway for the control number.

issue: Sequencing: far-eps sits in unit far-u2 (Area I), long before far-equity (unit far-u8). The EPS lesson assumes concepts taught only in far-equity: treasury stock, stock dividends vs. splits and cumulative vs. noncumulative preferred. Convertible bonds are not taught anywhere outside the EPS lesson. No prerequisite is declared, and the lesson gives no primer.
evidence: far.yaml order: far-u2 [..., far-eps] precedes far-u8 [far-payables, far-bonds, far-debt-other, far-equity]. far-equity/lesson.md teaches treasury stock (cost method), stock dividends and splits and cumulative preferred arrears (lines 10-34). In the EPS lesson these appear without definition (timeline, worked example, faded example). A grep for "convertible" in far-bonds and far-debt-other finds nothing.
fix: Either move far-eps after far-equity (e.g. to the end of far-u8), or add a 3-4 line "Before you start" primer to the EPS lesson. The primer would cover treasury shares (issued but not outstanding), stock dividends and splits (more shares, no resources), cumulative preferred (arrears carry forward) and convertible bonds (holder may exchange for common), linking to far-equity.

issue: Answer cue: all three distractors are absolutes ("Always included", "Never included", "Included only in basic EPS"), and the key is the only conditional. The key's wording "Included if met at period-end" is also looser than the rule.
evidence: cues.md flags absolutes only in distractors a, b and c. Under ASC 260-10-45-48 the test is whether the conditions would be met if the end of the reporting period were the end of the contingency period, and inclusion also requires the shares to be dilutive. The key's wording blurs this.
fix: Reword the key to "Included if the conditions would be met were the period-end the end of the contingency period (if dilutive)". Replace one absolute distractor with a plausible conditional, e.g. "Included only when the condition is probable of being met" or "Included from the date the condition is expected to be met".

issue: Trap labels do not match the misconception, or label the same misconception inconsistently across items. This degrades any misconception analytics.
evidence: 18(b) $4.00 deducts two years of cumulative dividends and is labeled "overgeneralization"; 03(c) labels the same error "wrong-period". 22(d) $5.60 adds the dividend instead of subtracting it and is labeled "distractor-number"; chk1(b) and 18(c) label that error "wrong-sign". "Shares repurchased reported as incremental shares" is labeled "reversed" in 04(d) and 25(b) but "wrong-classification" in 16(d). "Reports basic EPS as diluted" is labeled "partial-computation" in 08(c) and 20(a), "wrong-rule" in far-x1-08(d) and "wrong-classification" in far-x1-32(a).
fix: Use one label per misconception: two years of dividends -> wrong-period; adding a dividend -> wrong-sign; shares repurchased -> partial-computation (or wrong-classification) consistently; basic reported as diluted -> partial-computation consistently.

issue: The stems do not say that the securities and shares were outstanding all year (or that the share figure is a weighted average), and these answers depend on time-weighting.
evidence: 20: "100,000 shares are outstanding" and "convertible bonds with $50,000 of interest" give no period; if the bonds were issued mid-year, the add-back and the shares would be pro-rated. 25: "10,000 options ... average market price $25" gives no outstanding period. 27: "$1,000,000 of 5% bonds converts into 40,000 shares" gives no period. Comparable items 04, 05, 06 and 16 state "outstanding all year".
source: ASC 260-10-45 (treasury stock and if-converted methods apply from the later of the start of the period or the issuance date)
fix: Add "outstanding all year" (and "weighted-average" for the 100,000 common shares in 20) to each stem.

issue: The exhibit describes "Employee stock options" without saying they are fully vested. Under ASC 260-10-45-29, assumed proceeds for share-based payment awards include average unrecognized compensation cost. A well-prepared candidate could wonder whether that applies. The lesson and fc4 never mention it.
evidence: Keyed opt row = 15,000 - 600,000/60 = 5,000. That holds only if unrecognized compensation cost is zero, which the exhibit does not state.
source: ASC 260-10-45-29 (assumed proceeds include unrecognized compensation cost)
fix: Change the exhibit line to "Employee stock options (fully vested; no unrecognized compensation cost): 15,000 shares at $40", or relabel them "Stock options".
